AP: One social media comment on our coverage of this weekend’s event claimed: “There is no future for women’s boxing cos it is s****, basically.” It’s crass, but how would you respond to such a critic, and do you set out to prove people like that wrong – or just focus on hardcore boxing fans?

NB: “First and foremost, it’s a young sport. It only became an Olympic sport in 2012, the talent is improving every single year, and the US has never had women’s boxing at an Olympics they’ve hosted... but at LA 2028 we will have that, so that will further bring attention to the sport in a way we haven’t seen before.

“Secondly, we’re focused on two groups of fans. One is boxing fans who are now accustomed to seeing women’s boxing as well – and there’s some old, staunch guys who are like, ‘I’ll never watch it!’, but there’s lots of open-minded folks who say, ‘This is a lot more exciting, this is non-stop action.’ And two, we’re focused on female sports fans, women who consume women’s sports.

“If we’re just targeting the same pool as all the other promoters in men’s boxing, we’re kind of dead on arrival. Ultimately, if you don’t want to watch our product, that’s OK; we feel like we’re presenting the best in the world on a consistent basis.”

open image in gallery Emma Dolan training ahead of her world-title challenge against Irma Garcia ( Getty )

AP: This week, you signed a multiyear broadcast deal with Sky Sports, which has also just partnered with Zuffa Boxing. How do you fit in?

NB: “Our strategy and delivery to Sky is really focused on the women’s vertical, which is MVPW, and we announced our deal with ESPN a couple of weeks ago. So, to have ESPN in the US and Sky in the UK for women’s boxing is an incredible distribution platform to get as many eyes on these athletes as possible. The way we’ve structured those deals is to allow us to lead with the women but also have men on those cards, so it gives you the best of both – but really led by incredible female athletes.

“I think Zuffa coming further solidifies Sky’s investment in boxing. If it was just us, doing two or three shows a year here focused on women, that doesn’t give me the same excitement as Zuffa coming here as well and doing five, six, seven shows, because that just means there’s more investment internally at Sky. In terms of the writers, producers, social media, all of them will be more engaged, more active in supporting boxing on the whole.

“We’ve obviously taken a very specific strategy to focus on blockbuster live events and then really go deep on women’s boxing. We’ve done this because we believe you can actually have a referenced brand that’s female-oriented; it’s hard to do that on the men’s side, because you have promoters like Matchroom and Queensberry and PBC and Golden Boy and Top Rank... and now Zuffa. There’s an endless amount of premier promoters that focus 95 per cent of their energy on the men’s side.”

open image in gallery The legendary Amanda Serrano is the biggest name on MVP’s impressive female roster ( Getty for Netflix )

AP: Zuffa has been pretty controversial since its arrival in January. It’s seen as a major disruptor and has begun feuding quite aggressively with existing promotions, namely Matchroom. How do you view Zuffa?

NB: “It’s not that we love or have a problem with Zuffa. I think a lot of people are questioning their desire to introduce a Zuffa belt. For me, what’s important is having the best talent. You can’t just create a belt and say, ‘This is the best belt in the world and you should watch this, because you’re seeing the best talent in the world.’ No, the best talent in the world actually doesn’t currently sit in Zuffa on a mass scale. The ability of the belt to be successful depends on who the talent is.”

Landlord insurance can offer protection against damage caused by factors such as theft, vandalism, fire and flooding. It isn’t a legal requirement for landlords to have it. This week’s podcast picks have something for everyone.1. Safe

Streaming platform: All streaming platforms and YouTube

Genre: Society and culture

On this week’s episode of Safe, from the Youth Endowment Fund, host, youth worker and author Ciaran Thapar is joined by Grace Strong, director of prevention at Leicestershire Police.

Each episode usually brings together researchers, practitioners, campaigners and young people to discuss approaches to reducing violence and why it affects children and young people today.

Strong opens up about her journey from probation officer to community leader, why violence is a public health issue, and explains a groundbreaking way of working with young people.

She also discusses with Thapar what being safe meant for her as a child, the human connection that motivated her to continue her probation work, and why violence happens for many complex reasons.

Sadly, for many children, being affected by violence is a daily reality. Safe is a thoughtful podcast which explores why this happens and how we can solve it.

(By Yolanthe Fawehinmi)

2. A World With

Streaming platform: All streaming platforms

Genre: Culture and society

A World With is a podcast of personal monologues imagining alternatives to the systems we live in.

Host Sara Bafo records this episode from her childhood council home in West London, reflecting on housing, inequality, and what could be different. She weaves her own experience growing up in a large family among the reality of rising homelessness, despite thousands of empty homes across the capital.

This episode, with the idea of ‘no landlords’, questions their role and Bafo reframes housing as something to live in, not profit from, and offers grounded, practical ideas for change that feel both personal and possible.

“Homes have become trophies for investment, not places to live,” Bafo explains, which is a lasting thought as the nine-minute episode ends.

(By Sara Keenan)

3. Fashion Neurosis with Bella Freud

Streaming platform: All streaming platforms and YouTube

Genre: Fashion and wellbeing

For Bella Freud, a luxury fashion designer with a family legacy in psychoanalysis, becoming a podcast host seems only natural.

In the style of her great-granddaughter, Sigmund Freud, Fashion Neurosis encourages guests to recline on the sofa and engage in interviews structured like talk therapy sessions.

In the latest episode, Freud interviews Riz Ahmed, the award-winning actor and musician, who is promoting his latest Amazon Prime series, BAIT.

Straight away, the dulcet tones resemble more guided relaxation than a hard-hitting interview, but still, she manages to get her guests to open up. Even Ahmed surprises himself as he talks about the “magic of lying on the couch”.

You don’t have to be fashion-obsessed to enjoy the chat, but Freud enables Ahmed to analyse his fashion choices without really probing. The pair discuss code switching, and Ahmed talks about his green and white Reebok classics and how fashion choices intersect with heritage, colonialism and relationships.

Freud ensures the podcast is a two-way street, telling stories about her childhood and her design process, helping weave the conversation throughout.

The podcast covers a mixture of fashion, life, youth, arts, and so much more, showcasing some genuinely honest and interesting conversations.

(By Alexandra Snow)

4. A Voyage to Antarctica

Streaming platform: All streaming platforms and YouTube

Genre: Travel

A Voyage to Antarctica transports listeners to one of the most remote and unforgiving places on Earth.

In the second episode of its latest season, pioneering explorer Ann Bancroft reflects on a lifetime shaped by ice, endurance and exploration.

Bancroft, the first woman to ski to both the North and South Poles, speaks with a cool collectedness that makes even the most extraordinary achievements feel matter-of-fact.

Her relationship with Antarctica emerges as something more than a conquest and transforms into something innately personal as she describes a landscape that has challenged, humbled and ultimately defined her.

Instead of dramatising danger, Bancroft reflects on what it means to return to such an extreme environment and how it changes the way you see the world beyond it.

For those drawn to stories about resilience and perspective, this is the perfect podcast to get lost in.

(By Lara Owen)

Spotlight on…

5. Intelligent Machines

Streaming platform: All streaming platforms and YouTube

Genre: Technology

Have you ever thought about what will happen when AI inhabits all our devices, from cars and appliances to smartphones and robots?

In each episode of This Week in Tech (TWiT) podcast series Intelligent Machines, hosts Leo Laporte, Jeff Jarvis, and Paris Martineau will chat with the AI pioneers, inventors, and innovators who are about to disrupt every aspect of modern life.

They will explore some of the most exciting human revolutions, what these new devices will bring to our lives, and how to make the best use of them in the 21st century.

In the latest episode, tech journalist Marshall Kirkpatrick joins Laporte, Jarvis and Martineau to showcase a new AI-powered tool that doesn’t just summarise articles – it thinks like a journalist, flagging what’s truly new and revealing the patterns that matter.

If you want to stay several steps ahead in the AI race, Intelligent Machines is a must-listen.

The Artemis II astronauts ran into some tricky toilet trouble on the first day of their historic journey around the moon.

The crew saw a blinking fault light - like a “check engine” light in a car - shortly before performing a crucial step to send themselves into a higher orbit of the Earth overnight Thursday, above where satellites and the International Space Station reside.

The problem turned out to be a controller issue, Norm Knight, NASA's director of flight operations, told reporters at Florida’s Kennedy Space Center.

The toilet fan, which removes odor and airborne particles, was jammed, NASA spokesperson Gary Jordan said during the agency’s livestream of the mission, Space.com reported.

"Now the ground teams are coming up with instructions on how to get into the fan and clear that area to revive the toilet for the mission,” he said.

open image in gallery NASA's Artemis II Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft lift off from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center Wednesday. The four astronauts had to work to fix toilet problems on the spacecraft just hours later ( Getty Images )

The astronauts could still use the commode to poop - but not urinate.

"In the meantime they're getting their contingency - their backup waste management capabilities specifically for urine," Jordan said.

After mission control teams successfully assessed the data, they were able to fix the problem.

“The Artemis II crew, working closely with mission control in Houston, were able to restore the Orion spacecraft’s toilet to normal operations following the proximity operations demonstration,” NASA said in a statement.

open image in gallery The toilet is the first designed for a mission to deep space. It has a door, somewhat like these stalls which were designed for the International Space Station ( NASA )

The toilet, also known as the Universal Waste Management System, is the first designed for a deep space mission.

If the Artemis toilet cannot be fixed in the future for some reason, the astronauts will need to connect their urine in bags, according toThe New York Times.

For now, the Artemis team will continue to test their spacecraft’s capabilities and systems Thursday, before heading to the moon on day five or six of their flight.

News.title: ‘Amazing tasting, evenly cooked results in minutes’: The best pizza ovens, tested by our experts
News.content:
On the hunt for the best pizza oven to give to a foodie, or to get ahead for this summer’s al fresco dining? These days you can take your pick from hundreds of wood-fired, gas-fired and even electric pizza ovens. Wood-fired ovens deliver the classic smoky flavour preferred by traditionalists. Gas ovens are smaller, easier to use and offer better temperature control. Electric pizza ovens can cook more evenly.

Ooni leads the way, but Sage, Gozney and La Hacienda are also strong brands. At the top end sits Stefano Ferrara, whose domed, hand-bricked ovens appear in pizzerias worldwide, with prices starting at £6,000. For home cooks, you can achieve near-authentic results with a £300 model from Ninja.

We’ve tested all of these, among others, and you can read our reviews below, followed by answers to some frequently asked questions. But if you’re in a rush, here’s a quick look at our top five:

The best pizza ovens: At a glance

How to choose the best pizza oven

Matt Williams, Co-Founder of the The Oxford Charcoal Company, says the two things to factor is are size and fuel-type. Barbecue-top and portable pizza ovens which can run on gas or electricity are the best option for most homes, because they can be stored away more easily. If you want the best results, however, you do need a wood-fired oven.

“Being able to recreate that incredible wood-fired flavour and texture in your own garden is the ideal,” Williams says and for that, you’d probably need a wood-fired oven hot enough to cook a pizza in 60 seconds – which Italians will tell you is the best cooking time for a standout crust.”

Small wood-fired ovens are available, such as the Roccbox (reviewed below), but most are fairly large. All of the ovens in our guide will enable you to create a freshly-made pizza far superior to anything you’ll buy in a supermarket.

News.title: Alistair Brownlee: ‘I’ve been in a swimming pool zero times since retiring’
News.content:
How old were you when you started to compete professionally? Mary-Grace, East of England

I did my first triathlon when I was eight, but didn’t compete professionally until I was 18.

I won the World Junior Championships, and I did some serious races the year after I was 19. I went to the Beijing Olympics as a 20-year-old the year after.

What advice do you wish you would have received when you considered a career in sports? Ekaterina, London

My parents, my dad in particular, recommended that I studied alongside sport when I was young.

I also had some brilliant advice from my coach Malcolm, who told me to believe that I could win the Olympic games – but only by one stride, which was a great way of saying have faith but not too much, and train really hard.

Endurance sport, although it sounds a bit cliché, is a long game. Don’t rush things, look after your body, focus on the small things: nutrition, sleep, recovery, all of that, and that will pay dividends over a long period of time.

What was it like competing so hard against your brother and could you put the result to one side after the race was over? Caroline, East of England

I didn’t know any different. I’ve competed against my brother since I was really young – six-years-old or probably even younger in the garden at home so it’s very natural to me.

Even at the top level of the sport I think we took it for granted. We would be training side by side at home in Yorkshire one day and competing in the top races in the world the day after.

We basically knew that we were each other’s best training asset and we also knew that we could help each other in racing as well as the training.

We pretty much always put it aside straight after the race, and that was partly about our relationship and partly because we both had that kind of mentality, we were always thinking about the next thing.

Who was your biggest competitor and why? Nicolle, South East

Obviously my brother Jonny was a big competitor throughout the main part of my career.

I also had a very talented, ferocious Spanish competitor called Javier Gómez. I raced him probably 100 times during the same period. He came second at the London Olympics and beat me to the world title quite a few times.

We were very close in physical ability, and well matched in terms of where we were in the race. Quite a few of our races came down to sprint finishes.

News.title: Bompastor fury as hair pull goes unpunished in frantic end to Champions League tie
News.content:
McCabe pulled Thompson to the ground by her hair, leaving the Chelsea player upset just moments before Arsenal’s place in the semi-finals was confirmed by the final whistle. The incident happened just minutes after Sjoeke Nüsken scored in the 94th-minute to give Chelsea a brief glimmer of hope for a comeback.

Bompastor was still aggrieved in her TV interview with the BBC, arriving with phone in hand and a clip of the moment McCabe pulled Thompson’s hair asking the valid question: “Why do we have VAR?”.

She added: “I don’t want to speak to them [the officials] because it’s always the same story. Even if I go and speak to them, they will not give me a clear answer. It’s difficult for me because I don’t want to be the only one talking about this situation. Everyone needs to understand that’s the difference between being qualified and not being qualified. It has a big impact on players.”



McCabe, who has a track record of on-field incidents, took to Instagram after the final whistle to apologise, while the Arsenal players celebrated with music in their dressing room, with a message against a black background saying: “I just want to clarify that I was genuinely reaching for the shirt, I wouldn’t ever want to pull someone’s hair. Full respect to Thompson.”



However McCabe’s apology was dismissed by Bompastor, who insisted that the act itself was deliberate by the Arsenal full-back. She added: “She [Thompson] was crying. She’s trying her best on the pitch in both games and it is not good enough, when you are playing football and someone pulls your hair, it’s bad. Of course she was crying and emotional with the situation and the result.”

News.title: Marc Skinner calls on Manchester United to invest after ‘punch in the face’
News.content:
Manchester United head coach Marc Skinner says their elimination from the Champions League is the “punch in the face” the club needs to wake up to the gap in investment between themselves and their rivals.

United’s European journey ended at the quarter-final stage after they were beaten 2-1 by Bayern Munich in Germany, having lost the first leg 3-2 at Old Trafford last week.

The club’s exit from the competition came on the same day as the publication of their accounts for the 2024-25 season, which showed their wage bill was half that of Women’s Super League rivals Arsenal. United also spent far less on agent fees between February 2025 and 2026 than their competitors.

Asked whether the expectation on his team is too high given the gap in resources, Skinner gave a bullish response.

“I think we will learn from what investment is really needed to go into this level of competition for consistent years,” he said.

“I think we’re still learning as a club. I have incredible pressure, you know that, you read everything every day, sometimes you write it. I have incredible pressure and I hold that pressure. I want to say this, I’m incredibly proud of what my players are doing with the resources we have.

“Because we wear Manchester United’s badge, everybody expects us to be the very best team in the world. We have that expectation too. So that’s the pinch point, because we want to be the best. We’ve got to grow because we’re eight years old. We’re eight years old. You [can] give me all the flak, that’s fine, that’s no problem, that’s my job.

“But if we want to compete at this latter stage, we’ve seen what we’ve got to do, as a club. And then it’s our choice now, isn’t it? We have to look at what we seriously want to achieve and we’ll learn and grow from it. Even as a club, we’re still learning. It takes, sometimes, a punch in the face to wake up.”

United were without eight first-team players because of injury for this second leg but started strongly and deservedly took the lead after 11 minutes. Melvine Malard capitalised on a defensive error to finish into an empty net and bring her side level on aggregate.

News.title: Reeves backs North Sea drilling
News.content:
Rachel Reeves has backed drilling in the North Sea in a move that opens up a rift with Ed Miliband.

The Chancellor said she would be “very happy” to support extraction at two proposed new oil and gas fields because of the positive impact on “jobs and tax revenue”.

The intervention comes ahead of a decision by Mr Miliband, the Energy Secretary, on whether to grant licences for the Rosebank oil field and Jackdaw gas field.

Her comments put her on a collision course with Mr Miliband, who has banned new exploration in British waters and rejected pressure to extract more fossil fuels from the North Sea.

Asked if she supported drilling in the North Sea, Ms Reeves said: “I’m very happy that we are.”

“The North Sea oil and gas [will] play an important role in our energy mix for years to come, and we’re very lucky to have that resource and to be able to continue to use that resource.

“If we’re going to get ourselves off of this roller coaster of gas and oil prices, of course, we want to move to something that we have control over.”

It contrasts with Mr Miliband’s insistence that the only way to “get off the rollercoaster” is to abandon oil and gas altogether.

Meanwhile the SNP has u-turned on its opposition to further North Sea gas exploration in the aftermath of the war.

John Swinney, the First Minister of Scotland, said new fields should be permitted if the oil and gas they produced had a lower carbon footprint than imports.

The Chancellor’s comments come amid mounting pressure for Labour to reopen the North Sea as oil and gas prices surge as a result of the war in Iran.

Donald Trump urged the UK to “get your own oil” earlier this week and leading business figures including Octopus Energy boss Greg Jackson and British Gas chief Chris O’Shea have called for an expansion of North Sea drilling. Mr O’Shea said doing so “will bring prices down.”

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch this week launched a “get Britain drilling” campaign and Reform UK has also called for new North Sea exploration.

Ms Reeves told the BBC: “It would, of course, create jobs and tax revenue, and that is why we continue to support oil and gas for decades to come.

“We have now got the disruption in the Middle East, and it’s hard to get the oil and gas out of the Strait of Hormuz, which is pushing up prices. It does show that we have got to take control of our own energy supplies here in Britain.”

The Chancellor said the only reason drilling had not begun at Rosebank and Jackdaw was that courts overturned licenses granted by the previous government.

She said: “We said in our manifesto we would honor existing licenses, but the courts overturned the previous government’s decision. That is not the fault of this government, but we’ve had to go through the processes to be able to do it lawfully.”

Executives have said the fields could be producing fuel within months. Mr Miliband imposed new delay on the licence approval process by demanding new information from operators in recent weeks.

Ms Reeves also said she is “angry” that Donald Trump launched the Iran war without a “clear plan” in the most direct criticism of the president from a Cabinet minister yet.

She told the BBC: “I’m angry that Donald Trump has chosen to go to war in the Middle East – a war that there’s not a clear plan of how to get out of. It’s why we didn’t want to enter this.”

Sports.title: Dark history of DR Congo’s last World Cup under different name, from pay row to being ‘threatened’ by president’s guards
Sports.content:
THE Democratic Republic of Congo are heading to the World Cup for the first time in 52 years this summer.

But the last time they went to the tournament, their country had an entirely different name.





Former Manchester United stars Axel Tuanzebe and Aaron Wan Bissaka were two of the pivotal stars that helped lead the African nation back to the World Cup, with the former scoring the winning goal against Jamaica in the play-off to secure their place.

Back in 1974, Zaire would become the first Sub-Saharan African country ever at the World Cup Finals – the very same year the country held Muhammed Ali vs George Foreman in Rumble in the Jungle.

Although Egypt was the first African country in a World Cup back in 1934, it wasn’t until 1974 a black African country made their bow.

It’s believed that’s mostly due to years of rejected applications and qualification rules put in place by FIFA that seemingly made things far more challenging for the Sub-Saharan teams



From just after gaining independence from Belgium in 1960 to 1971, the country was known as Congo. Dictator Mobutu Sese Seko – we’ll call him Dictator Mobutu – renamed it Zaire, but once he was overthrown in 1997, the country re-emerged as the Democratic Republic of Congo.

While all laws and power sources were being centralised by the new Zaire government led by Dictator Mobutu, the country had progressed through a gruelling qualifying phase that saw just one African side earn a place at the World Cup in West Germany.

They beat much-fancied Morocco 3-0 in a decisive final group stage match and went on to win the African Cup of Nations followed at the start of 1974.

Despite the turmoil at home, underpinned by the First Congo War that started in 1966, Zaire had become a formidable force in the world of football.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They didn’t have Premier League stars like Tuanzebe and Wan-Bissaka in their ranks in those days. Although there was a few singular cases, the mass migration of African stars to top European sides didn’t start in earnest until the 1980s and 90s.

But they did have the ‘Black Beckenbauer’ Tshimen Bwanga. They also had AFCON ’74 top scorer Ndaye Mulamba, who was the captain of the team at the finals.

These days, fans have been spoilt with the rich talents that have come out of the African continent, whether it be Roger Milla and his seductive hips at Italia ’90, Jay-Jay Okocha running amok at USA ’94 or even Senegal shocking France to kick off the 2002 iteration of the event.

Mohamed Salah is one of the most famous footballers on earth. Yaya Toure is one of the all-time great Premier League midfielders, as is Didier Drogba when it comes to strikers. The lists go on and on.

But the world was far smaller in 1974. This was before social media, scouring networks and, well, the internet!



So Zaire arrived in West Germany as an unknown quantity, but touted as potential surprise packages.

They had the task of taking on the formidable Brazilian team of the 1970s, a Scotland team with Kenny Dalglish and Dennis Law among others and a dangerous Yugoslavia outfit, but they were not short on belief.

They opened up against the Scots, who struggled to deal with the energy and pure attacking intent.

Scotland may have underestimated them, but they managed to escape with a 2-0 win which many argue was against the run of play.



Zaire, led by their Yugoslavian coach Blagoje Vidinic, would then face his home country in their next outing. What unfolded next left a stain on African football for a myriad of reasons, but perhaps what transpired was misunderstood in real time.

Dictator Mobutu was understandably elated when the team qualified for the tournament. Excited to project his vision of Congo’s African strength, the dictator allegedly bought all of the players new houses and cars.

He also set up a deep cash kitty for the players to dip into during the tournament if they needed it and an enormous entourage of government and Zairian football officials to accompany the team.

However, after just the first game, it was quickly realised the kitty was nearly gone thanks in large part to all of the sticky fingered officials who had flown over.



The players soon discovered this and not only learned that their World Cup fund was nearly bled dry, but that cash reserve was supposed to be their wages and bonuses for the tournament, too.

Furious with the betrayal from their own people, a large part of the Zaire squad decided they would not play against Yugoslavia and go on strike. This caused FIFA to intervene and pay the players 3,000 deutsche marks themselves, if only to save the tournament from embarrassment.

What followed was a Zaire team bereft of pride or desire reluctantly taking to the pitch. They would lose 9-0 to Yugoslavia, tied-first for the heaviest defeat in World Cup finals history.

Did they throw the game after backstabbing turmoil in their own camp? Did they fail to prepare and, bereft of enthusiasm, suffer the consequences? Or were they simply handed a lesson on the pitch?



It’s hard to say. But what the eyes could see was a sloppy display. Either poor players or players who looked poor. It was an embarrassing look for Zaire and African football, lending credence to those who looked down on them to begin with.

Scotland manager Willie Ormond had said: “If we can’t beat Zaire then we should pack our bags and go home.” That’s what the footballing world thought.

But would it have been worse if the world knew the real struggles going on behind the scenes? That might have been even worse for their image.

So the world was kept in the dark at first and there was one more encounter to deal with before their World Cup was over – facing the champions Brazil.



Zaire had become the joke of the World Cup by this point. Already eliminated and on the end of a history-making beating; the idea of facing one of the best Brazil sides was the worst possible tonic.

You won’t be surprised to learn that someone like Dictator Mobutu was not thrilled with being humiliated. He decided to get involved again.

Fullback Mwepu Ilunga has since claimed in an interview given to the BBC that the Brazil game quite literally became life and death.

“After the match, he sent his presidential guards to threaten us. They closed the hotel to all journalists and said that if we lost 0-4 to Brazil, none of us would be able to return home.”

Why 4-0 is the magic scoreline for Dictator Mobutu, we don’t know.



Then comes the moment that has made every World Cup highlights package ever since.

Brazil held a 2-0 lead over the tournament first-timers in the final Group B match. Just 10 minutes remained when the legendary duo of Rivelino and Jairzinho stood over a free-kick.

But, before they could take it, Zaire defender Mwepu Ilunga broke from the wall, sprinted at the Brazilians and hoofed the ball up field.

Ilunga was surely unaware he was about to attain football immortality and to the naked eye, it looked like somebody who didn’t truly understand the rules of the sport he was playing.



BBC commentator John Motson even called it “a bizarre moment of African ignorance.”

But it wasn’t ignorance. It wasn’t stupidity, either. It was fear. It was a time-wasting tactic designed to confuse Brazil as the Zaire team knew they could not afford to lose 4-0.

Brazil did end up scoring again, but the game finished 3-0 and the Zaire team was safe to return home – but not welcomed.

From national heroes to shamed, penniless, outcasts; almost every career of the players was instantly over.

Mobutu swiftly changed his tune on football. He cut funding to the national team and the sport became almost frowned upon in the country for a generation.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now, Congo rises from the ashes of the suppressed Zaire to take its place in the newly expanded 48-team World Cup. They will be one of 10 African teams at the finals and they have many players operating in the top leagues around Europe.

Congo is now a nation reconnected and they’re ready to re-write their nation’s story.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Fede Valverde was urged to have surgery for rare throat problem that made him sound like Mickey Mouse
Sports.content:
REAL MADRID star Fede Valverde was forced to undergo throat surgery after a rare condition left him with a high-pitched voice likened to Mickey Mouse.

The midfield powerhouse revealed he struggled for years with the issue, with doctors repeatedly telling him he needed an operation but his family simply couldn’t afford it at the time.





Valverde said during an interview on Terapia Picante: “When I spoke, I had a problem in my throat and I was always advised to have surgery.

“We were a humble family and couldn’t pay for an operation overnight.

“We thought it was just something from adolescence, that it would change, but it never did.”

The problem became the subject of online jokes after a clip of him aged 17 at Club Atletico Penarol went viral, with fans mocking his squeaky voice and comparing him to Mickey Mouse.

Thankfully, the issue has now been resolved, with Valverde admitting: “Now it has changed, thank God- but at the time I suffered.”

Despite the setback, the Uruguay ace has gone on to become one of the biggest stars in world football, even captaining both club and country in 2026.

But his journey to the top was anything but smooth.

Valverde also opened up on feeling completely out of place after arriving in Madrid as a youngster, admitting he was “crushed” by the culture shock.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “I thought, ‘I don’t know what I’m doing here.’ My teammates had amazing cars and designer clothes- I didn’t want to even take mine off in the dressing room.”

On the pitch, though, it was a different story.

Known for his thunderous shooting, Valverde even revealed he once injured Luca Zidane, son of Zinedine Zidane, leaving him fearing the worst.

He admitted: “I was devastated. I thought they were going to fire me.”

He recently scored a hattrick against Manchester City that helped Madrid progress to the quarter final of the Champions League.



His impact at Madrid has left many again hailing the club’s scouting system having brought him in early just as they did with Vini Jnr and Rodrygo.

Sports.title: Chelsea boss makes rarely-seen move in furious post-match interview after being sent off in Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
FUMING Chelsea boss Sonia Bompastor was so angry at a bad refereeing decision she got out her phone during the post-match interview to prove how clear the incident was.

Bompaster held up her phone to the BBC cameras as evidence of what she thought should have been a red card for opponents Arsenal.





The decision wasn’t given and Chelsea were knocked out of the Champions League quarter-finals by their London rivals.

Arsenal looked set to have Katie McCabe sent off when the full-back pulled the hair of Alyssa Thompson during a Chelsea attack in added time.

Despite VAR being in play, the Gunners escaped punishment – leaving Blues boss Bompastor seething.

So angry was the Chelsea boss that she herself was sent off by the referee.

In her post-match chat on the BBC, Bompastor pulled up game footage of the Ireland captain grabbing Thompson’s hair.

Bompastor said: “I brought the phone with me, I don’t know if you can see that.

“But if you look at this video, for me it’s clearly the red card for the Arsenal player. She’s pulling Alyssa’s hair.



“I just think it’s not good enough.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“At the end I’m the one who gets a red card where I think the Arsenal player should be the one who gets a red card.

“What is the VAR doing in these games? If we have the VAR, why are we not checking these situations?

“I don’t understand, and it’s not good enough.”

The French manager initially saw yellow for her touchline protests, but was soon sent down the tunnel.



Bompastor added: “At the end, I’m the one who gets a red card, where I think the Arsenal player should be the one who gets a red card.”

Chelsea were trailing 3-1 after the first leg.

The second leg ended 1-0 to Chelsea after Sjoeke Nusken scored the only goal of the game in the 94th minute.

If it wasn’t for McCabe’s hair pull, the Blues would have had one last opportunity to find an equaliser.

But the hosts didn’t get that chance and ultimately lost 2-3 on aggregate and were eliminated from the Champions League.



McCabe wrote on socials: “I just want to clarify that I was genuinely reaching for the shirt, I wouldn’t ever want to pull someone’s hair.

“Full respect to Thompson.”

In the first leg of the quarter-final, Stina Blackstenius, Chloe Kelly, and Alessia Russo put three past the Blues at the Emirates.

Lauren James recovered one for Chelsea as the tie ended 3-1.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Holders Arsenal will now progress to play either Lyon or Wolfsburg in the first leg of the Champions League semi-final on April 25.



They face each other tonight in France, but Wolfsburg lead after a 1-0 win in the first leg.

Sports.title: I tried out VR technology Odegaard is using to get back to his best for Arsenal – his brain is so fast it left me dizzy
Sports.content:
MARTIN ODEGAARD has missed over 120 days of action this season through injury, but fortunately for Arsenal, he is using cutting edge tech to keep sharp for his return.

The Gunners captain, 27, leans into the world of Virtual Reality to keep his brain match-sharp without any physical burden during his rehab.





Odegaard, who is fighting to return from a knee injury in time for Arsenal’s FA Cup quarter-final with Southampton on Saturday, is one of a host of modern-day pros focusing on training their ‘scanning’ to improve their game.

Scanning – how a player takes in information on the pitch – has become one of the most useful skills in football, with so many of the top players lauded for how they can paint a picture of the game around them before they even receive the ball.

And it’s a big reason why Odegaard is still fourth for chances created per 90 minutes in the Premier League this term, behind only Bruno Fernandes, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki.

The Norwegian is the king of reading the game and knowing exactly where his team-mates – and opponents – are at any given moment.



Part of that is down to his use of Be Your Best, a handy piece of VR tech that simulates in-game situations and trains players in scanning using AI and cognitive science.

Odegaard was the first of a wave of pros to adopt the software, which was developed after research showed the best players in the world are those who can scan the most.

Now, over 10,000 players, including Aurelien Tchouameni, Marc Guehi and Romeo Lavia, use it to better their game.

In its simplest terms, scanning is the process of taking small glances away from the ball to check your surroundings, but for the elite players it means they are always one step ahead of their opponents.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Be Your Best CEO Andreas Olsen thinks that edge can be the difference between being a great player and a world-class player.

Olsen told SunSport: “We believe that we will play an important part in the journey of a player, and we can be an accelerator to improve your cognitive skills. That’s what we are striving for.

“When it comes to the pro players, like Tchouameni, before he started to use it, he was already at a good level.



“But for him, improving by just one per cent can actually mean the difference between becoming a really world-class central midfielder for Real Madrid and being a good central midfielder for Real Madrid.”

Tchouameni first started using VR ahead of a game he played at centre-back for Real Madrid, wearing the headset to get used to playing in the backline and the situations he would face from those positions on the pitch.

For Odegaard, the tech is about making his return to the pitch feel easy.

The team at Be Your Best had to introduce their own ‘Odegaard Mode’ that simulates a Premier League level game at 120 per cent speed, after the Arsenal ace maxed out the previous settings with ease.

Odegaard wanted something that would make his return to action feel slow in comparison to the rehab work he had been doing.



SunSport got their hands on the industry-leading tech and even got the chance to try out ‘Odegaard mode’, with the fast-paced scenarios leaving us dizzy and unable to realise we even had the virtual ball at our feet at times.

The tech, which 80 different clubs have adopted, registers how often players scan and whether they can carry out what is called a ‘critical scan’.

A critical scan is defined as a final glance away from the ball while a pass is already on its way to a player.



Odegaard is brilliant at this, and was even seen advising Arsenal academy kids to take ‘one last look over your shoulder’ when receiving the ball in a clip from his recent documentary.

Over the course of a game, Odegaard scans almost 500 TIMES on average, meaning he is constantly taking in information about what is around him.

In the 10 seconds leading up to the ball arriving at his feet he looks away roughly seven or eight times, far more than the three to four times an average Premier League player glances away.

It’s why the midfielder so often looks like he has far more time on the ball than he actually does.

Mikel Arteta will be hoping that Odegaard’s extracurricular activities will help him slot straight back into action ahead of a crucial run-in for the Gunners.



With Ebere Eze ruled out for several weeks due to a calf injury, Odegaard’s creativity could be the key to Arsenal finally getting over the line in their quest to end a 22-year wait for a league title.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Despite six different injuries hampering his ability to play consistently this season, Odegaard still ranks first for assists per 90 and second for passes into the final third per 90 at Arsenal this season.

And with his VR training only helping him stay sharp, Arsenal fans will be hoping he will rediscover that form as soon as he gets back out on the pitch.

Sports.title: Premier League club to add new Wembley feature to 49,000-seat stadium and fans can be a part of it
Sports.content:
SUNDERLAND have gone from strength to strength after coming up from the Championship this season.

And now they’ve taken another step forward.





The Black Cats will transform the Roker End plaza into a new fan hub dubbed Legends’ Way, celebrating iconic players, moments, and supporters.

Legends’ Way is set to transform the exterior and hand fans the chance to claim a permanent spot in the club.

Future fans will arrive on match day and be welcomed at the heart of the Wembley Path with a wall of stones decorated with messages.

They’ll be able to buy their own engraved stone for anything between £99 and £500.



Supporters will also be able to choose where it sits on the wall, whether it’s near one of the statues or bordering one of the 14 Legend Stones.

These Legend Stones will be selected via a fan vote.

But the transformation doesn’t stop there.

Jimmy Montgomery – the club’s record appearance-maker and 1973 FA Cup hero – will be immortalised alongside boss Bob Stokoe, recreating the famous Wembley moment.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Sunderland‘s huge plans are set to be completed ahead of the 2026/27 season.

And Roker Park’s ‘Welcome to Sunderland’ sign will feature on this side of the stadium for everyone to spot on match days.

Sunderland will be full of confidence on the back of the 2-1 victory in the Tyne-Wear Derby as they continue their fight for European spots.

Sunderland – who sit 11th in the league – have the chance to move into ninth if they beat Tottenham at home next Sunday.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi team up again as Real Madrid stars join them in star-studded World Cup advert
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO and football foe Lionel Messi have teamed up in an advert crawling with huge names.

Ronaldo, 41, and Messi, 38, are set to do battle at the World Cup later this year.





And they have spent their careers scrapping each other for Ballon d’Or supremacy, with Messi leading eight to five.

But this time they joined forces, along with Real Madrid superstars Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior, for a star-studded LEGO advert.

The plastic construction toy company launched their FIFA World Cup collection on Instagram and there was football royalty at every turn.

Fans will get the chance to build the World Cup trophy and tributes to all four players.



The advert shows Ronaldo putting the finishing touches on the LEGO World Cup trophy before Vinicius nips in to place the penultimate piece.

Mbappe then places the final piece before all four stars scramble to put their own LEGO figure on top of the silverware.

Fans can build Ronaldo, Messi, Mbappe and Vinicius tributes in the ‘Football Highlights’ set, and Ronaldo or Messi in the ‘Football Legend’ set.

Ronaldo said: “It’s not every day you get to be transformed into a LEGO set!



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I’m incredibly honoured to be part of this new lineup of LEGO Editions, alongside three other incredible players in the sport.

“I’m looking forward to seeing fans from all over the world discover my story and sporting heritage by building this LEGO set, blending football and creativity.”



Messi added: “Similar to football, LEGO play is all about building and rebuilding, trying new things, learning from mistakes and celebrating successes.

“I love how these LEGO sets bring my on-pitch moments to life in a fun and imaginative way.

“I’m thrilled for fans to explore the magic of football through these sets and together celebrate the sport we all love.”

Sports.title: Man Utd bosses fear new transfer issue thanks to Andre Onana contract clause
Sports.content:
Man Utd bosses fear new transfer issue thanks to Andre Onana contract clause

Andre Onana could land himself a hefty Manchester United pay rise despite being absent all season with a likely return to the Champions League seeing the squad benefit financially

View 2 Images Man Utd were happy to let Andre Onana leave in the summer, but face an imminent decision on his future (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United's charge towards the Champions League could see Andre Onana land a pay rise despite being absent all year - and it could make it all the more challenging to offload him in the summer.

‌



The Red Devils have been without the Cameroon goalkeeper for almost the entire season following his shock loan departure to Turkish side Trabzonspor. There was no obligation or option to make the move permanent, meaning he is set to return to Old Trafford in July.

‌



Onana was signed by Erik ten Hag in 2023 but he was part of a squad-wide pay cut that occurred after United failed to reach Europe for the 2025-26 campaign. It meant the players got hit with a 25 per cent reduction, so as to offset the lack of European revenue.

‌



But United sit third in the table and a return to the Champions League would see the players' salaries return to their original levels. The Sun reports that figures at United are concerned that the increase in salary will make it more challenging to get Onana off their books.

Man Utd told Elliot Anderson would fancy Newcastle return over Old Trafford switch READ MORE :

The player himself though, who previously played in a Champions League final with Inter Milan, is determined to stay and fight for his place in Manchester.

United signed Senne Lammens from Royal Antwerp for £18million in the summer when he was relatively unknown, but he's since established himself as their No 1. The Belgian has impressed and now commands the jersey.

‌



A return for Onana could leave United having to carry a very expensive goalkeeper as their back-up. Should they want to send him out on loan again they may have to pay a portion of his salary just to get him off their books. They currently have the luxury of Trabzonspor paying his entire salary.

View 2 Images Andre Onana is currently on loan at Trabzonspor (Image: Gerrit van Keulen/Getty Images)

United's willingness to move Onana on for the year came after two error-strewn years, which eventually saw him dropped for a brief period by former boss Ruben Amorim. After replacing David de Gea, despite his ability to play out, it quickly became evident that he was not as good a shot stopper.

Article continues below

Amorim said on his exit: “Sometimes it’s hard to point where things went wrong. The performance, the moment, the bad luck in some moments was hard on him. I wish the best for Andre. He was really hard working and good at helping the players. But sometimes you need to change the environment.”

Sports.title: Casemiro shows up Ruben Amorim with striking comment on Man Utd team-mate
Sports.content:
Casemiro shows up Ruben Amorim with striking comment on Man Utd team-mate

Kobbie Mainoo is a key part of Michael Carrick's Manchester United side after struggling for game time under former manager Ruben Amorim.

View 2 Images Casemiro has made his feelings on Man United teammate Kobbie Mainoo clear (Image: Manchester United/YouTube)

Casemiro has appeared to disagree with former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim on Kobbie Mainoo, naming his teammate as ‘one of the best’ in his position. The Brazilian's comments flew in the face of what Amorim had said about Mainoo previously, insisting he could be the world's best for the next 12 years.

‌



Mainoo found himself on the sidelines under Amorim and was unsure of his future at the club, even contemplating a loan or permanent exit amid interest from Chelsea and Napoli. He has, however, been reintegrated into the starting lineup by interim manager Michael Carrick and has been flourishing for the club again.

‌



The academy graduate has started every game under the stewardship of Carrick, which earned him a place back in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the current international break. Mainoo featured in both friendlies against Uruguay and Japan and will be bidding to earn a place on the plane for this year’s World Cup.

‌



Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged READ MORE :

Premier League clubs ranked as Man Utd left in the dust by rivals cashing in on academies READ MORE :

Under Amorim, Mainoo failed to start a Premier League game this season, with his only start coming in the shock Carabao Cup defeat against Grimsby Town. It led to Mainoo pushing to leave the club in the summer window.

But the 20-year-old's immediate impact since coming back to the fold post Amorim has shown up the club's former boss. Several big-name pundits and club icons were baffled at his lack of game time and now Casemiro has twisted the knife by tipping him to go on to stardom.

“Kobbie is the present and the future,” the Brazilian said in a Q&A with United. “I think that he is one of the best No.8s and can be for that for the next 12 years.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“He is a player I really like. He always wants the ball. It is true that football can’t change your mentality but Kobbie demonstrated that he hasn’t changed his focus once.

“He has to continue focusing like he is now and continue playing the important role he is now. But what a player he is, he is a great player.

‌



"He has demonstrated this, in the Euros final with England, he has demonstrated it in finals, he scored in the FA Cup [Final, vs Man City in 2024]. Kobbie is the present and the future.”

When questioned back in December why Mainoo wasn’t getting game time, Amorim bit back. "You always ask me the same thing,” he said.

"I understand what you are saying. You love Kobbie. He starts for England, but that doesn't mean I need to put Kobbie on when I feel I shouldn't."

‌



View 2 Images Kobbie Mainoo has been an ever-present in Michael Carrick's starting line-up for Manchester United. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Steven Gerrard is among the pundits to have recently blasted Amorim’s treatment of the player . “I felt really sorry for him in terms of the kid’s career under Amorim,” he told TNT Sport.

“I think it was out of order that he never got any opportunity, especially with Man United being so inconsistent.

Article continues below

“But not surprised that Michael Carrick [started to play him]. I think that was one of the straight wins if you walk into a job, if you like. Get Kobbie Mainoo back in, get him smiling, give him game time and minutes, and get him fit and up to the speed where we all know he can play.

“He’s now at a level where he walks in the England squad, never mind Amorim not playing him. He walks into the England squad if he’s playing regularly for Man United.”

Sports.title: Arsenal urged to beat Chelsea in summer transfer race for ex-Real Madrid star
Sports.content:
Arsenal urged to beat Chelsea in summer transfer race for ex-Real Madrid star

Como ace Nico Paz, who was once of Real Madrid, has shone for the Italian side and Arsenal have been encouraged to pursue the Argentine despite interest from the likes of Chelsea

View 2 Images Nico Paz has excelled in an impressive Como outfit

Arsenal have been urged to land Como's Nico Paz this summer despite former club Real Madrid having a buy-back option and Chelsea also being keen.

‌



The Gunners have continued to invest heavily in their squad and, more recently, spent big to land the likes of Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze. They have helped spearhead their pursuit of the Premier League this term.

‌



Now Owen Hargreaves thinks they should go after Paz, who has been a shining light in a Como side that have exceed expectations in Serie A. They sit in the Champions League spots with the Argentine midfielder scoring 11 times in all competitions.

‌



Paz, who is managed by former Arsenal star Cesc Fabregas, has been at the Italian side since 2024 when he left Los Blancos. The Spanish giants are believed to have the option to re-sign Paz but Hargreaves thinks Arsenal need to move for the 21-year-old, who could see his stock rise at the World Cup this summer.

The former England star said on TNT Sports: "There’s a young lad at Como, Nico Paz. There’s an option for him to go back to Real Madrid but if I’m Arsenal… This kid – you’ll see him at the World Cup. Mikel Arteta will already know that this boy will be a star and if you don’t ask you don’t get. A player like that could suit Arsenal."

Nico enjoys playing, he can play different roles and he is very complete player. I see a very, very big potential in him."

Arsenal may have to make several decisions regarding their frontline this summer. Ethan Nwaneri has had to head out on loan with Mikel Arteta struggling to give all of his players their desired game time.

Sports.content:
FIFA world rankings confirmed ahead of World Cup with new No.1 after England lose

The field for World Cup 2026 is now complete with the international break over and there is a new World No. 1 topping the FIFA rankings

View 3 Images England were beaten 1-0 by Japan to end the latest international break (Image: Getty)

England remain fourth in the FIFA world rankings after a lacklustre international break. But it's all change in the World No. 1 spot with Spain supplanted.

‌



The Three Lions entered this break with friendly games against Uruguay and Japan on their doorstep. Their opening fixture at Wembley ended in a disappointing 1-1 draw, after Ben White's late goal was cancelled out by Federico Valverde's penalty in second-half stoppage time.

‌



Japan were up next and a much-changed England starting XI failed to break them down. Thomas Tuchel's side were beaten 1-0 thanks to a goal from Brighton's Kaoru Mitoma.

‌



However, despite these sub-par results, England have retained fourth place in FIFA's rankings. The same can't be said for a host of other teams and there is now a new No. 1.

England supporters warned of ‘huge’ human rights risks at 2026 World Cup READ MORE :

Spain held the World No. 1 position heading into this international break. But after the Euro 2024 champions beat Serbia 3-0 last week, they were held to a 0-0 draw by Egypt.

‌



View 3 Images Spain were held by Egypt (Image: Getty)

This result has seen them drop to second in the rankings, with France taking over the top spot. Les Bleus beat Brazil 2-1 last month before a convincing 3-1 victory over Colombia.

Argentina round out the top four in third. This quartet will all be seeded at the upcoming World Cup and won't be able to meet each other until the semi-final stage. Portugal, Brazil and the Netherlands dwell just outside the top four, with the highest-ranked African nation in the rankings being Morocco in eighth.

‌



Italy remain in 12th place, despite their catastrophic playoff loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina meaning they won't be competing in North America come the summer.

The hosts of the competition all rank within the top 30, with the United States at 16th, Mexico at 15th and Canada at 30th. The same cannot be said for other home nations.

View 3 Images Wales were defeated on penalties in Cardiff (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Wales were another team to suffer qualification heartbreak at the hands of Bosnia and they have dropped two places to 37th in the rankings. Scotland will be at the World Cup but their international break was poor enough to drop them five places to 43rd.

The Republic of Ireland were eliminated from World Cup contention by Czechia but remain at 59th in the FIFA rankings. Sports.title: Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged
Sports.content:
Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged

Manchester United were left fuming that Amad was denied a penalty in their draw at Bournemouth, leading to an official complaint, but a Premier League panel has now backed the referee's decision

View 2 Images Man Utd were left fuming that they weren't awarded a penalty at Bournemouth

Manchester United have been told that both the referee and video assistant referee (VAR) were right to wave away Amad's controversial penalty appeal in their draw at Bournemouth last month.

‌



The Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has ruled on the decision, which left the United players and Michael Carrick stunned, and believes that the officials made the right call.

‌



Amad went down inside the area after Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert appeared to place two hands on him. Referee Stuart Attwell waved away the penalty appeals - with the visitor's anger only increasing when the Cherries went up the other end and scored through Ryan Christie in the 67th minute.

‌



United's frustration peaked as Matheus Cunha was given a penalty, which was then converted, for a challenge that looked extremely similar to the one Amad was on the receiving end of. The Red Devils made a formal complaint to the Premier League regarding the decision.

Since then the KMI Panel produced a split 3:2 vote against a spot-kick being awarded on the field. It was claimed that "whilst Truffert runs a risk, the contact made was not impactful and therefore below the high threshold for a foul". However two panellists said the action was "non-footballing" with a penalty the right call.

Harry Maguire charged by FA for reaction to Man Utd red card against Bournemouth READ MORE :

Matheus Cunha responds after Man Utd complaint and Harry Maguire fury READ MORE :

Despite those opinions the KMI Panel unanimously supported the VAR staying out of the situation, stating that it was "in keeping with the high threshold for VAR overturns".

‌



United would concede a late equaliser from the spot, which only added to Carrick's frustrations. He told Sky Sports: "We should have had another penalty. Obviously, if you get one, you must get the other. It's pretty much identical for me, two-hand grab. Either way, [the ref] got one wrong, but to give one and not give the other, I can't get my head around it. I think it's crazy. It's a bit baffling, really.

View 2 Images Amad saw his penalty appeals waved away (Image: Sky Sports)

"Because of that, they score and then it's chaos after that, really. We should have had another penalty and the game would have been totally different."

‌



Bruno Fernandes echoed that sentiment as he said: "We get a penalty against [us] where more or less it's the same situation as Amad. One is rewarded as a penalty, the other one not. I know it's difficult for the referee to give two penalties in the same game for the same team but what I don't understand is why VAR doesn't get involved in that situation.

"Either one is a penalty and the other one too or none of them is a penalty."

Sports.title: 'I made up my mind on Roberto De Zerbi after watching him take a training session'
Sports.content:
'I made up my mind on Roberto De Zerbi after watching him take a training session'

Roberto De Zerbi has been appointed as the new manager of Tottenham and a former Spurs star has offered a strong review of the Italian

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi's training sessions have made quite an impression (Image: Getty Images)

New Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi has been handed a resounding endorsement from Danny Murphy. On Tuesday, Spurs confirmed De Zerbi's appointment, with the Italian agreeing a five-year contract to succeed Igor Tudor, who left by mutual agreement just two days prior.

‌



De Zerbi gained significant acclaim during his two seasons at Brighton, where his team developed a reputation for playing some of the most intricate and exciting football in the Premier League. However, although the 46-year-old's forward-thinking approach was eye-catching, there are now doubts about whether his philosophy suits a relegation dogfight.

‌



Spurs sit just one point above the relegation zone with seven matches remaining, offering very little time to adjust to a different playing style. That said, Murphy expects De Zerbi to take a practical approach over the coming weeks.

‌



"I'd be amazed if I see Spurs go to Sunderland in his first game and start trying to play through the Sunderland press in front of their crowd. No, he's not daft," the former Tottenham midfielder said on talkSPORT.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Tottenham Supporters' Trust issue damning statement after Roberto De Zerbi appointment READ MORE :

"He's got to get them to the summer and keep them in the Prem. And then what you'll see is a progression of Tottenham's football and a definitive way of playing."

‌



Murphy also shared that he had attended several Brighton training sessions during De Zerbi's tenure and left very impressed. "The sessions were quality," he said.

"He was doing a session where they were working through the lines and the intensity he had and what he was demanding, the football was good and I liked what I said. And speaking to him, he had a presence, he had a bit about him. You know when you're with someone and they've got a bit of an aura, some grit, some believe in himself, some gravitas.

"I remember watching his Brighton teams and thinking, 'They know what they're doing, you can see that they've been coached and they've got a method.'

‌



View 2 Images Murphy was a big fan of De Zerbi's Brighton team (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

"Now, I'm not sure that method is going to be the way to go in these next six, seven games. I'd be loathe to do that... he hasn't got the time, it's dangerous."

With Tottenham already out of the FA Cup, De Zerbi has over a week to train with his new squad before his first match against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. Spurs will then welcome his former side Brighton to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium six days later.

‌



In a video message directed at supporters, De Zerbi said: "It's a very big honour and I'm very proud to be your coach. I want to give my best and I want to stay for a long time in this big club."

Tottenham's interest in De Zerbi dates back to 2023. The club stepped up their pursuit in February after Thomas Frank was dismissed, which happened on the same day De Zerbi left Marseille by mutual agreement.

It is believed De Zerbi was initially hesitant about taking the job mid-season, preferring a move in the summer, leading Spurs to appoint Tudor instead. However, following further talks in March, he was convinced to step in immediately.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

"In all my discussions with the club's leadership, their ambition for the future has been clear - to build a team capable of reaching great achievements and to do that playing a style of football that excites and inspires our supporters. I am here because I believe in that ambition and have signed a long-term contract to give everything to deliver it," De Zerbi said in a statement.

"Our short-term priority is to climb the Premier League table, which will be the complete focus until the final whistle of the last game of the season. I'm looking forward to getting out on the training pitch and working with these players to achieve that."

Article continues below

Sporting Director Johan Lange added: "Roberto was our number one target for the summer and we are very pleased to be able to bring him in now.

"He is one of the most creative and forward-thinking coaches in world football, and brings with him a wealth of experience at the highest level, including in the Premier League."

Sports.title: Premier League clubs ranked as Man Utd left in the dust by rivals cashing in on academies
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs ranked as Man Utd left in the dust by rivals cashing in on academies

Manchester United, Chelsea and Manchester City are among the clubs to make big money from sales of academy players over the last few years.

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho moved from Manchester United to Chelsea in the summer transfer window. (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Manchester United have been left trailing Chelsea, Manchester City and Aston Villa after new figures on academy sales were released. United’s academy has become renowned over the years for producing some of the best talent in the world.

‌



However, former manager Ruben Amorim was critical of the academy talents coming through despite the emergence of the likes of Kobbie Mainoo, JJ Gabriel, Ayden Heaven and Chido Obi over the last few years - and when it comes to making profit off their young players, the club are far behind some of their rivals.

‌



Selling academy products has become an important process for Premier League clubs, as they are treated as pure profit under the Profitability and Sustainability Regulations (PSR). Therefore, any fee from the sale of a player who has come from the academy can be recorded in full on the club's books, which is a boost when complying with the rules.

‌



Despite the positive reputation around the United academy, the latest weekly post from the CIES Football Observatory has the club in 19th place among clubs worldwide that have made the most profit from the sale of academy players over the last 10 years. In terms of Premier League clubs, United are in fourth, behind Chelsea, City and Villa.

If just looking at English clubs, Chelsea lead the way with the most money made from sales of academy products. The Blues have brought in £386million through 33 sales, with Mason Mount's exit to United accounting for 16 per cent of that .

Behind Chelsea are Man City with a total of £353m raised from 35 sales. Their biggest sale was Cole Palmer moving to Chelsea, which accounted for 12 per cent of the total.

‌



The next Premier League club is Aston Villa, although they have only made 13 sales; Jack Grealish’s move to Manchester City accounted for 39 per cent of their £265m total.

Manchester United are the fourth English club on the list, having earned £237m from 30 sales from the academy. Alejandro Garnacho’s move to Chelsea back in the summer was the biggest of those moves, accounting for 17%.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Just behind United are Arsenal, with a total of £236m. Like United, that total is from 20 sales, with Alex Iwobi’s move to Everton in 2019 bringing in the most from a single sale.

Tottenham are not far behind. Spurs have made £234m over the last 10 years. That comes from 19 sales, with Harry Kane’s move to Bayern Munich accounting for 45 per cent of the total.

Liverpool are slightly further down the list, having made £194m from 22 sales. The biggest of those was Jarell Quansah’s move to Bayer Leverkusen back in the summer.

‌



View 2 Images Jarell Quansah moved from Liverpool to Bayer Leverkusen in the summer transfer window. (Image: Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images)

When looking at the list as a whole, Benfica top it, having banked a staggering £514m through 38 sales. Their biggest sale was Joao Felix’s transfer to Atletico Madrid in 2019.

Ajax are second on the list, with a total of £396m from 43 sales. Their biggest fee received was from United for defender Matthijs de Ligt.

‌



Chelsea are then in third place on the list. Lyon, Sporting CP, Real Madrid, AS Monaco, Pakmeiras and Bayer Leverkusen also all appear in the top 10.

If the filter is changed to the last five years, then Chelsea, City and Villa take the top three spots, having made £320m, £278m and £256m respectively. United are seventh on the list, having made £192m.

Sports.title: Donald confirms 'rock of support' to return as Ryder Cup vice-captain
Sports.content:
Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald has confirmed Edoardo Molinari will return for a third stint as a Team Europe vice-captain at next year’s contest in Ireland.

Donald will attempt to become the first Ryder Cup captain in history to win three consecutive editions of the biennial contest, with the former world No 1 confirming Molinari will be part of his backroom team at Adare Manor next September.

Molinari will once again provide statistical support to Donald and Team Europe through his statistical analysis model, which helped them to a 16.5-11.5 victory in Rome in 2023 and a historic 15-13 away win at Bethpage Black last September.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Donald revealed to Sky Sports the process that saw him accept a third stint as Team Europe's Ryder Cup captain

"Edoardo [Molinari] has been a rock of support to me," Donald said. "He has made such a difference to our team. He is invaluable from a statistical analysis perspective, in terms of helping me with the qualification system, navigating the ever-changing world of golf.

"He is a very steady head. I always know where I stand with him and he gives me great advice. My vice-captain appointments are important, so to have his expertise again is key. He is a major factor in our backroom team.

Image: Luke Donald has welcomed Edoardo Molinari back for a third stint as Ryder Cup vice-captain

"He is a numbers guy and he is always looking at how to gain those edges, through statistics, through looking at the golf course and how you can set it up to give yourself just a little bit of an edge, which you have a little bit more control over as a home team."

Molinari was a winner with Team Europe as a player at Celtic Manor in 2010, prior to back-to-back spells as vice-captain, with the Italian relishing the opportunity to return to support Donald in the centenary edition of the Ryder Cup.

"It was a very easy decision when Luke [Donald] called me and asked me if I was willing to help him again," Molinari said. "I was obviously very happy. Any time you can get involved in the Ryder Cup, in any role, it's a great thing and I cannot wait for Adare Manor to come soon enough.

"Luke is an unbelievable captain. He's very well-liked by all the players. The great thing about him is that he leads by example. He really puts a lot of effort and thoughts into this process.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy says Europe will benefit from having Luke Donald as captain for the third consecutive time in the Ryder Cup

"He [Donald] is trying to make all the players very comfortable when they're in the team. At the same time, he's very motivated to win. He will really try any new avenues, new ideas, and see what works. He is incredibly hardworking. the players really follow him because they see how motivated he is."

Donald will name further vice-captains ahead of the next year's Ryder Cup, having used Thomas Bjorn, Jose Maria Olazabal and Francesco Molinari in his European backroom team for both previous editions.

Tiger Woods' decision to withdraw from Ryder Cup consideration leaves Team USA facing questions over who will lead them into next year's edition at Adare Manor.

Woods was initially favourite to succeed Keegan Bradley for the centenary edition in Ireland, with the former world No 1 in discussions with the PGA of America over the role in the months prior to his latest car crash on March 27.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after the second round of The Players, former USA Ryder Cup captain Keegan Bradley suggested he's open to a return to the role in the future

The 15-time champion was charged with driving under the influence and announced on March 31 he would step away from golf for a period to focus on his health, with the PGA of America confirming a day later that Woods' decision also ends the possibility of him being Team USA's next captain.

Webb Simpson, Brandt Snedeker and Jim Furyk were among Bradley's vice-captains at Bethpage Black and are possible contenders for 2027 captaincy, with Stewart Cink and Justin Leonard also options.
